what_it_is: Antonov State Enterprise is Ukraine's transport-aircraft designer, creator of the An-32 twin-turboprop airlifter that forms a backbone of the Indian Air Force's tactical transport fleet, and the An-124 heavy airlifter used for outsized cargo. The company was historically the OEM for Indian An-32 support, overhaul and upgrades.
india_angle: India operates a large An-32 fleet and has pushed depot-level overhaul indigenisation through 1 BRD Kanpur and 3 BRD Chandigarh, with public reporting targeting full Indian overhaul by FY2028-29 - a deliberate de-risking from Ukrainian OEM support disrupted by war. An-32 safety and availability remain sensitive issues in Indian public debate.
intelligence_assessment: Antonov's India relevance is defensive: sustaining a legacy fleet while India localises its support. The indigenisation roadmap is verifiable through Indian media and IAF statements; Antonov-side programme participation post-2022 is increasingly opaque.

faq.q: Why is Antonov in an India military-aerospace atlas?
faq.a: The IAF's An-32 transport fleet is Antonov-designed; India is localising its overhaul at 1 BRD Kanpur and 3 BRD Chandigarh.
